reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown split the one word 'tempt' into solicitation to evil, which God never does, and testing that proves faith, which is what happened to Abraham.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells lists Genesis 22:1 against James 1:13 as a straightforward contradiction, noting that the King James Version uses the same word 'tempt' in both verses.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com).

sides.verseText: It happened after these things, that God tested Abraham, and said to him, \"Abraham!\" He said, \"Here I am.\"

sides.snippet: for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
sides.verseText: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
